departement.description: Nominated by the executive board, the Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the economic success of the airline and reports to the executive board.
Responsible for aircraft purchasing/leasing, financial management, accounting, and procurement activities.
Responsible for the airline's business decisions: long-term strategy (business model, alliances) and short-term (routes).
Responsible for the airline's corporate image, press releases, media interface, airline website and internal staff communications.
departement.note: Corporate Communication is a key member of the Emergency Response Plan (ERP).

departement.description: Responsible for identifying new routes and frequency opportunities, and proposing route network and schedule modifications.
departement.note: For implementation of the above, a good relationship with Flight Ops Engineering is key.

departement.description: Responsable for managing the overall customer experience and defining the "onboard product" including entertainment/meals.
departement.note: In some airlines, Passenger Services may be a top-level department reporting directly to the CEO.

departement.description: Responsible for managing route profitability by monitoring load factors, setting prices and monitoring markets and destinations;
Responsible for managing customer claims and compensations.
Responsible for managing external relationships with other companies (including airlines) and defining corporate identity and direction.
departement.note: This department manages external relationships with other companies (including airlines) and defines corporate identity and direction. It is responsible for strategic partnerships and commercial alliances.

departement.description: Responsible for including corporate governance, environmental impacts, working conditions and ethical responsibilities in the airline's strategy.
departement.note: RSE = Responsabilité Sociétale des entreprises

departement.description: Responsible for aircraft purchases/leases, insurance, accounting, management control and cash flow.
Responsible for contracts, staff welfare, discipline and recruitment.
departement.note: RH = Ressources Humaines. Pilot/stewardess recruitment is qualified as "bulk" due to high volumes of personnel and the constant nature of selection criteria. For "bulk" recruitment, HR will work closely with the crew sizing department, the fleet pilot chief/cabin crew director and the crew training team.

departement.description: Responsible for telecommunication tools, software administration and cybersecurity. Manages all software programs used by the airline.
departement.note: SI = Système d'information. Some programs are essential for the airline's operation (fleet and crew scheduling, DCS). If they stop, aircraft are grounded and the company will lose cash flow.

departement.description: Responsible for ensuring the organization complies with information security regulation requirements.
Provides emergency technical assistance to resolve software and hardware issues, ensuring operational continuity. It's the first point of contact for daily technical problems.
Responsible for administration and relationship with the supplier of IT tools used by the airline: DCS, Ticketing, Fleet and crew planning, Flight planning, Management tool, Document library.
departement.note: The Product Managers team handles administration and vendor relationships for critical IT tools such as DCS, ticketing, and fleet/crew planning systems. These systems are essential for daily operations.

departement.description: Responsible for all matters concerning national laws related to commercial, civil and criminal law.
departement.note: In smaller airlines, the legal department may be attached to another department, for example the Commercial Department.

departement.description: Responsible for delivering service to customers: operating aircraft to transport passengers and cargo. The Accountable Manager is responsible for establishing and maintaining the management system.
departement.note: The AM establishes and promotes the safety policy according to Air-Ops regulations and the information security policy according to Part-IS regulations. Their name and profile are notified to the civil aviation authority.

departement.description: The Compliance Monitoring Manager (CMM) is responsible for demonstrating compliance of operations about safety to the Civil Aviation Authority to get and maintain certificates and approvals. The CMM put in place and maintain an internal and independent surveillance programme (audits and checks). Very often, he's also responsible for the compliance monitoring with information security regulation requirements.
departement.responsable: Compliance Monitoring Manager (CMM) [Responsable Surveillance de la Conformité (RSC)]
departement.note: In small organisations, the CMM may be the same person than the SM. His/her name and profile are notified to the Civil Aviation Authority.

departement.description: Responsible for the airworthiness of fleet aircraft and supervision of their maintenance.
departement.responsable: Continuing Airworthiness Nominated Postholder (CAPH) [Responsable Désigné Maintien de Navigabilité (RDMN)]
departement.note: His/her name and profile are notified to the Civil Aviation Authority. This department cannot be subcontracted legally.

departement.description: Accountable Manager is the final responsible for safety and compliance to Part-145 regulatory standards.
departement.note: Subcontracted maintenace (Part-145)

departement.description: Responsible for scheduled inspections at home base requiring grounding the aircraft for some time and heavy unplanned maintenance tasks.

Responsible for demonstrating compliance of maintenance about safety to the Civil Aviation Authority to get and maintain Part-145 certificate. He/she put in place and maintain an internal and independent surveillance programme (audits and checks).
departement.note: If the Part-145 is integrated to the airline, the Part-145 Compliance Monitoring Manager may be the same person than the CMM.

departement.description: Responsible for daily inspections performed on aircraft at outstations, for example during nightstops, and light unplanned maintenance tasks
Responsible for risk management and occurrence investigations for the MRO.
departement.note: If the Part-145 is integrated to the airline, the Part-145 Safety Manager may be the same person than the SM.

departement.description: Responsible for managing aircraft parts stock ("Store") and purchasing new aircraft parts.
Responsible for maintenance tasks planning and aircraft status follow-up.
departement.note: The Civil Aviation Authority certificates CAMO and approuves CAMO manager name and profile. This department cannot be subcontracted legally.

departement.description: Responsible for respecting all maintenance task time limits and optimizing maintenance planning, taking into account unplanned maintenance tasks.
Maintenance Control Center (MCC) is an operational department responsible for monitoring maintenance execution in real time. It works closely with the OCC.
departement.responsable: Compliance Monitoring Manager [Responsable Surveillance de la Conformité (RSC)]

departement.description: Responsible for answering technical questions about aircraft maintenance in emergency and coordinating maintenance tasks with operations.

Responsible at one or more stations for providing technical support and advice on aircraft maintenance and repair activities, conducting inspections and audits to verify MRO compliance with safety protocols, and assisting in troubleshooting technical problems.
Responsible for designing and implementing crew training and control programs. Responsible for crew competency level.

departement.note: His/her name and profile are notified to the Civil Aviation Authority. Very often, the CPTH is under the FOPH but he/she shall keep direct access to AM.

departement.description: Responsible for ensuring an ERP is in place and promoted to all necessary staff.
departement.note: Gestion de crise

departement.description: Responsible for operating flights with the highest safety, security standards and also good operational performance, punctuality, economic efficiency and service quality.

departement.note: His/her name and profile are notified to the civil aviation authority.

departement.description: Responsible for coordinating ground assistants at stations. Ground Operations Nominated Postholder (GOPH).

departement.note: His/her name and profile are notified to the civil aviation authority.

departement.description: Responsible for risk management and occurrence investigations.
departement.note: In small organisations, the SM may be the same person than the CMM. His/her name and profile are notified to the Civil Aviation Authority.

departement.description: Responsible for demonstrating security compliance of operations to the civil aviation authority to obtain and maintain certificates
departement.note: In small organisations, the Security Manager may be the same person as the CMM.

departement.note: Experienced pilots responsible for the Flight Data Monitoring (FDM) program and safety culture promotion. Although not regulatory, this role exists in all airlines.

Crew training engineers are responsible for keeping up-to-date and compliant crew training documentation, following FSTD (Flight Synthetic Training Devices) status, provide the CTPH with financial information in order to allow a budget control and follow-up and participating in every projects of CTPH.

TRE (Type Rating Examinators) are FC who have the privilege to extend the validity of FC licences upon succesful tests (initial and recurrent tests). SFE (Synthetic Flight Examiners) are TRE but cannot fly and only perform exams in simulators.

TRI (Type Rating Instructors) are FC who have the privilege to train FC to develop or reinforce their skills before or after a test (initial and recurrent trainings). SFI (Synthetic Flight Instructors) are TRI but cannot fly and only train in simulators. GI (Ground Instructors) deliver theorical and practical training in classrooms.
Cabin crew instructors are cabin crew who train and evaluate cabin crews (initial and recurrent trainings).
departement.note: Very often, cabin crew training is managed by the Cabin Crew Director (but stay under the responsibility of CTPH).

departement.description: Responsible for establishing and maintaining Evidence-Based Training system for Flight Crew He/she uses training data to monitor crew proficiency level and improve the training program performance.
Crew training assistants are administrative agents who are crucial to conduct operations. They monitor crew license validity, plan crew training sessions and keep training records.
Responsible for CRM (Crew Resource Management) training.
